title: multi-wave-canary-orchestration-and-shadow-sweep-blueprint
text:
multi-wave-canary-orchestration-and-shadow-sweep-blueprint

description:
Objective: Create a repeatable, automated blueprint for running multi-wave canaries that combine synthetic load sweeps and production shadowing (request duplication) to validate model and routing changes before progressive traffic ramp. Scope includes orchestration policies, metric gating matrix, synthetic harness definitions, shadow sampling strategies, and runbook-level escalation paths.

Why: Existing canaries either rely solely on production metrics (slow to surface regressions with low traffic) or on synthetic unit tests (miss real-world signal). By combining short synthetic load sweeps with targeted production shadowing in discrete waves, we can reduce time-to-detect regressions while keeping blast radius low and enabling deterministic rollback triggers tied to SLOs and quality thresholds.

Deliverables: blueprint doc, orchestration policies as config (for the rollout controller), synthetic test harness templates, shadowing client patterns and rate controls, gating matrix implemented in console with per-metric thresholds, and an operator runbook with automated escalation hooks.

acceptance_criteria:
Blueprint doc describing wave definitions, decision tree, and rollback thresholds is published and reviewed by Eng/Design/SRE/Legal
Rollout controller supports 'multi-wave' primitive with shadowing and synthetic steps in config and passes unit tests
Synthetic harness repo contains at least 3 scenario templates (latency tail, hallucination/regression prompt set, token-growth cost regression) and is runnable in CI with results surfaced to the experiment dashboard
Console displays gating matrix with live pass/fail state for canaries using configured thresholds
Runbook includes automated escalation steps, contact list, and postmortem obligations and is validated in a fire-drill
Security review completed and customer data leakage risk from shadowing is documented and mitigated (masking/KMS, PII scrubbers enabled)

metrics:
Primary safety SLOs: user-facing tail latency P99, 95th-cost-per-1000-tokens, error-rate (5xx + model-failure), and hallucination-rate (measured via eval suite)
Quality signals: semantic-similarity regression delta on canonical prompt set, instruction-following score, high-confidence divergence rate
Operational signals: inference CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, KV-cache hit rate, model memory paging events
Business signals (optional): downstream conversion lift delta, churn proxy metrics for top customers in trial

rollout_plan:
Wave 0 - Synthetic sweep (off-prod): run 30m stress and quality checks at scaled qps; if any critical threshold crosses, block wave progression
Wave 1 - Shadow sweep (1% traffic duplication): duplicate a sampled 1% of production requests to the candidate model; results are only logged and compared asynchronously
Wave 2 - Shadow + reduced routing (5% routed, 10% shadow): route 5% live traffic to candidate with 10% shadow duplication for quality amplification
Wave 3 - Progressive ramp (25%, 50%, 100%): after passing gating windows for 30m at each step, automate ramp; include heartbeat canary checks every 5m
Rollback: any safety SLO or critical quality threshold breach triggers immediate automated rollback to previous pinned model and alerts the on-call chain

monitoring_and_alerting:
Experiment dashboard with per-wave aggregated metrics and per-prompt example sampling
Auto-alerts: P99 latency increase >20% sustained for 10m, hallucination score delta >5% absolute, customer-impacting error-rate spike >0.5%
Health checks: synthetic job heartbeat; if missed for two consecutive runs, hold progression
Tracing hooks: request-level tracing for any routed requests during waves 2-3 to speed debug

graceful_degradation_policies:
Fallback routing: automatic reroute to baseline model on resource pressure or uncaught exceptions
Token budget guarding: cut mid-request generation if cost delta exceeds configured threshold to prevent runaway billing
Feature flags: ability to disable shadowing or synthetic steps per-customer in Dedicated/Private deployments for compliance

risks_and_mitigations:
Data leakage from shadow duplication - mitigation: apply PII scrubbing and KMS encryption for shadow logs; limit retention to 7 days
False positives in synthetic tests causing unnecessary rollbacks - mitigation: calibrate synthetic thresholds using historical regressions and require cross-signal agreement before automated rollback
Increased load on serving runtime during canaries - mitigation: reserve burst capacity pool and implement rate limits on synthetic generator clients
Operational complexity for customers on Private - mitigation: provide an opt-in 'managed canary orchestrator' and clear docs for on-prem config

comments:
2025-10-07 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes - aligned with SRE on synthetic harness compute budget and with Legal on shadowing PII constraints; agreed to prototype with two internal customers in Dedicated environment.
2025-10-22 | Marco Rivera: Draft orchestration YAML added to design doc; prototype controller accepts 'waves' list, each wave has type (synthetic|shadow|routed), duration_mins, sample_rate. Need Eng signoff on API shape.
2025-11-03 | Priya Menon (SRE): SRE review passed at high level; asked to add explicit guard for KV-cache warming to avoid cold-start spike during wave transitions.
2025-11-10 | Legal (L. Chen): Completed privacy checklist; approved shadow logging with PII scrubber and 30-day retention (we elected 7-day retention for safety).
2025-11-18 | Marco Rivera: Security review flagged audit logging for shadow duplication; added requirement to surface replication events in Console audit trail. Planning a small spike to prototype audit events.
2025-11-21 | Aisha Patel: Decision - proceed to eng spike for controller and synthetic templates. Next milestone: eng deliver spike PR and a working demo with one internal customer by 2025-12-01.
